s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative sepsis with signs of peripheral hypoperfusion and coagulopathy
salient_findings: Tachypnea, tachycardia, and fever
Cyanosis of fingers and toes with low peripheral oxygen saturations
Ecchymoses and easy bleeding from puncture sites
Necrotic and septic right groin wound
Progression to well-demarcated gangrene below the elbows and knees
key_facts: 14-year-old boy
Postoperative wound sepsis after right scrotal exploration and orchidectomy
24 hours of scrotal pain and swelling before surgery
Tachypneic, tachycardic, febrile, and diaphoretic on arrival
Pallor of mucous membranes
Normal heart sounds and flat neck veins
Cyanosis of fingers and toes with peripheral oxygen saturations between 20% and 30% on room air
Ecchymoses over the extremities
Easy bleeding from puncture sites
Necrotic and septic right groin wound
White blood cells 16 × 10^3/µL with neutrophils 10.8 × 10^3/µL
Hemoglobin 4.8 g/dL
Platelets 26 × 10^3/µL
Normal liver and renal function tests, electrolytes, malaria smear, and hemoglobin electrophoresis

shortlist.label: Purpura fulminans
shortlist.why_kept: Postoperative wound sepsis, ecchymoses, and easy bleeding suggest coagulopathy

shortlist.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
shortlist.why_kept: Lab results show low platelets, low hemoglobin, and evidence of bleeding

shortlist.label: Meningococcemia
shortlist.why_kept: Sepsis, fever, and rash-like symptoms could be indicative of this condition

shortlist.label: Severe sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's condition, including fever, tachycardia, and tachypnea, aligns with severe sepsis

shortlist.label: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
shortlist.why_kept: Low platelet count and evidence of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia
